installation.note: alias is a shell built-in (bash, sh, etc.)

overview.summary: alias defines a shortcut name for a command or command string. Typing the alias runs the defined command. Without arguments, alias lists current aliases. Aliases are session-only unless added to .bashrc or similar.
when_to_use: Create a shortcut for a long or often-used command
Add default options to a command (e.g., alias ls='ls -la')
List current aliases (alias with no args)

syntax.description: alias NAME=VALUE defines an alias. alias alone lists all aliases. alias NAME shows that alias.

examples.title: List aliases
examples.description: Show all defined aliases in the current shell

examples.title: Make alias persistent
examples.description: Add alias to .bashrc so it loads in new shells

related_commands.description: Shows if a name is an alias, function, or binary
